title: As Mossad chief visits US, fears grow Netanyahu could strike Iran to block Eisenkot
author: Ben Caspit
text:
Analysis

As Mossad chief visits US, fears grow Netanyahu could strike Iran to block Eisenkot

Israel's opposition leaders fear that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could exploit the transition period to reignite the Iran conflict, thereby delaying or even preventing the formation of a new government.

Ben Caspit

Nov 13, 2026

Add AL-MONITOR on Google

Iranians take part in a military course for volunteers at a training camp for women at the Azadi Square in Tehran on Nov. 10, 2026. — Atta KENARE / AFP via Getty Images

عربي简体中文Español

TEL AVIV — Israeli opposition leaders fear that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could provoke Iran into reigniting a military confrontation to prevent the formation of a new government under his rival, Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot, Israeli political sources told Al-Monitor.Citing three sources familiar with the matter, Axios reported Friday that Mossad Director Roman Gofman is currently in Washington. According to the report, he met with CIA Director John Ratcliffe, is expected to meet with Secretary of State Marco Rubio and might travel to Miami to meet with White House envoy Steve Witkoff as part of Netanyahu’s efforts to press President Donald Trump to resume military operations against Iran.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu meets Mossad chief Roman Gofman at the Mossad headquarters on Aug. 31, 2026. (Prime Minister's Office)

The political uncertainty in Israel and Trump's continued zigzagging on Iran are adding to tensions among Israelis who are already exhausted by three years of war and the inconclusive results of the Oct. 27 elections, the sources said.Eisenkot received the recommendations of 67 Knesset members, surpassing the 61-seat majority threshold and leaving just 46 for Netanyahu. On Sunday, President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming the next government. However, negotiations with potential coalition partners have proven difficult. During the 42-day transition period, Netanyahu remains in power as caretaker prime minister.
